evidence.supportingExcerpt: Format changes what is tested. A soluble molecule must stay intact and usable through manufacture, storage and exposure, and adding binding units or a chemical cargo can change its behaviour (Junutula et al., 2008, anti-MUC16 conjugate in mice, rats and monkeys). A CAR fixes the binder to a membrane and links contact to signalling, so spacer reach, target position, expression and clustering matter (Hudecek et al., 2015; Long et al., 2015). The same recognition sequence therefore does not guarantee the same performance.

proofs.requirement: Isolated affinity or one architecture does not establish universally better activity, safety or efficacy.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: The manufacturing evaluation includes molecular identity, correct pairing, aggregation, fragments, stability and biological potency. Affinity, binding kinetics, avidity, target distribution and exposure belong to the actual format. Two successful binding assays do not by themselves demonstrate the intended combined function.

Generation labels describe common signaling architectures. First-generation constructs use an activation domain, often CD3 zeta; second-generation designs add one costimulatory region; third-generation designs combine two. Fourth-generation and later labels vary across authors. More domains do not establish better patient outcomes. The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.

evidence.supportingExcerpt: A change of format is a new product hypothesis. If an ADC binds M but yields little active material after uptake, an M-directed engager might avoid that particular processing requirement. It still needs its own binding and contact-geometry measurements, useful effector access and function, normal-tissue testing and clinical evidence. Earlier antibody or ADC tolerability does not establish the safety of a different action. Bystander delivery and two-address designs are possible responses to heterogeneous expression, not guaranteed coverage or an exhaustive list of solutions.
